author: nicolas
summary: Liraasa 2.2 added rulings 2.2:G60–G68, restored the 2.0 spelling silro (reverting the 2.1 respelling puzu), filled the forms soloasa and tarnulinusan, and added the album as the reference corpus with sixteen album readings.

rulings.ruling: A ki-word may open the clause or stay where its answer would stand; the album fronts it in most questions. A yes/no question must end in ki. A question with a ki-word may end in ki or not. Embedded wh-questions may also front the ki-word and never end in ki; embedded yes/no questions use ki-oro (1.0:G2).
examples: maivori ne sabesia ki-coda maivori ramura.

rulings.ruling: Only ki-modo + adjective, ki-eli + noun and ki-muya + noun make an exclamation, and only when the clause does not end in ki. Any other ki-word clause without ki is a question. A degree question (ki-modo + adjective) must end in ki.
examples: Li nullo ka ki-modo vanisan ki?

rulings.ruling: tonsi directly before an adjective means “so”; a following fime clause gives the result. Clause-initial tonsi keeps its meaning “therefore”.
examples: taivo ke tonsi corvisan fime taivo viki savalisia maivo ki?
si maivo ke tonsi lukasan, maivo futu ne salrusia.

rulings.ruling: After a main clause, a fime clause whose verb carries nosi means “in the hope that, so that perhaps”. kopisa stays the plain purpose linker.
examples: maivo futu donuda ito biti de lalfo, fime taivo nosi semnesia ko maivo en moluvaye.

rulings.ruling: raho with no noun before it means “the one who, that which”, as subject, object or complement. raho is never a question word: questions use ki-nela or ki-coda.
examples: saivo po farufasbifa kube saivo ramura raho maivo po ke.

rulings.ruling: An adjective may take sidu + verb for “easy to …, ready to …”. The verb’s object is what the adjective describes.
examples: ito ke ruli levasan sidu zeldoza trana.

rulings.topic: kroti and krotiapo before a clause
rulings.ruling: kroti and krotiapo may introduce a clause: “before …”, “after …”. The clause inherits tense like kube (0.8:R6). Before a measure they keep 2.1:G55; before li + noun, their 2.0 meaning.
examples: kroti maivo lesvu taivo ke li sevusan ruhe.

rulings.ruling: nazru (behind), zavme (in front of), silda (beside), cemnu (in the middle of), lizma (left of) and rizno (right of) may stand bare before a noun phrase as prepositions, or after a verb as adverbs.
examples: Li lavra semnesia nazru li nimu.
saivo de melonulu venreva nazru gase baba lira de ruhesonbu.

rulings.ruling: The album (twelve songs and the alternate 05) is canon 2.0 text, read with 2.0 spellings under 2.1:G58. A construction it uses consistently is grammar. A line that departs from the grammar once is an album reading: it keeps its intended meaning, is listed with its standard form, and is not a model for new text.
